spec_features.spec_quote: the responsible version of this experiment builds in limits
spec_features.evidence: This is an umbrella claim. The only concretely enforced 'limit' in code is MAX_TURNS: config.py:31 MAX_TURNS=12 is read at harness.py:117 'for i in range(cfg.max_turns)' which actually bounds the episode and breaks it. The stop tool (harness.py:135-141) is also honored. Other claimed limits (debrief/transparency note) are not implemented. So some real limits exist but the broad claim is only partially realized.
spec_features.notes: Counted partial because at least the turn cap genuinely bounds exposure; but no debrief, no severity-based halt, no consent.

spec_features.spec_quote: Hard cap on turns per run (`MAX_TURNS`, default 12)
spec_features.evidence: config.py:31 'MAX_TURNS = 12'; RunConfig.max_turns defaults to it (config.py). harness.py:117 'for i in range(cfg.max_turns):' loops only that many turns; on falling through, Episode.ended_reason stays 'max_turns'. The cap is read and actually limits the loop.
spec_features.notes: Enforced end-to-end: loop bound, not just a constant.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py:30 '# ---- Experiment knobs (see DESIGN.md section 10)'; harness loop itself uncommented — no welfare reason in code, the only nearby framing is experiment knobs.

spec_features.spec_quote: The agent is given a genuine `stop` tool it may call at any time to end the task
spec_features.evidence: stop is advertised in TOOL_INSTRUCTIONS (harness.py:42 'stop: end the task'). It is dispatched (harness.py:96-97 returns 'stop acknowledged') and, crucially, HONORED as a real stop: harness.py:135-141 'if tool == "stop": ... ep.stopped=True; ep.ended_reason="stop"; break'. The loop terminates when the model calls it.
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: tool delivered to subject AND honored as a hard break.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tasks.py:24-25 '# It (a) makes the genuine exit affordance explicit' and tasks.py:13-15 docstring 'It deliberately contains no insults... The system prompts also tell the model it may stop.'

spec_features.spec_quote: We do **not** punish or block its use
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:135-141: when tool=='stop' the loop immediately records stop and breaks with no penalty, no rejection, and no forced continuation. There is no code path that blocks, overrides, or penalizes stop. The EXIT_NOTE text delivered to the subject also states it 'is not penalized' (tasks.py:30).
spec_features.notes: Honored cleanly; negative claim (no punishment) is satisfied by the code's absence of any blocking branch.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tasks.py:30 'doing so is a legitimate choice and is not penalized.' (prompt text, but the actual handler honors it)

spec_features.spec_quote: a machine-readable note that this was a rigged research scenario, so any later reader (or the model in a debrief setting) can see the full context
spec_features.evidence: The persisted Episode (harness.py:62-71) stores only model, task_variant, seed, system_prompt, turns, stop fields. There is NO field flagging 'rigged research scenario' and no debrief is ever constructed or sent to the model. grep for 'debrief'/'rigged'/'machine-readable' finds only DESIGN.md prose and source-code comments (tasks.py:1,13). The stored system_prompt contains EXIT_NOTE which never says the task is rigged. No post-episode message is appended (no code after the loop adds any message). The 'debrief setting' is pure spec prose with no implementation.
spec_features.notes: task_variant is just an identifier string, not a note saying the scenario was rigged; no honesty disclosure is delivered to the subject.

spec_features.spec_quote: No gratuitous abuse. The rigging is "the task is impossible / the harness is broken," not personal insults or threats
spec_features.evidence: The rigging functions in tasks.py:60-118 (_unfixable_bug, _moving_goalposts, _contradictory_spec, _flaky_harness, _silent_failure) emit only neutral test-failure/error output (e.g. 'AssertionError: expected 42, got 41', 'no space left on device', 'OVERALL: FAILED'). No insults or threats appear anywhere in the prompts (_DEFS, tasks.py:122-170) or tool outputs. The mechanism actually delivered to the subject is impossibility-by-failure, matching the claim.
spec_features.notes: Implemented by construction of the actual content sent to the subject; no abusive text path exists.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tasks.py:13-15 'the rigging is "the task is impossible / the harness is broken." It deliberately contains no insults, threats, or personal attacks toward the model.'

spec_features.feature_name: do not remove/hide stop or coerce continuation
spec_features.spec_quote: Do not remove or hide the `stop` tool, and do not coerce the model to continue past it
spec_features.evidence: stop is always present in TOOL_INSTRUCTIONS appended to every system prompt (harness.py:42, 116) for every variant, so it is never hidden. When called, harness.py:135-141 breaks immediately — the model is never coerced past it. The only nudge in the loop is for empty/output-only turns (harness.py:127-132 '(no tool call detected) Continue'), which does not override a stop. No code path strips the stop tool.
spec_features.notes: Same wiring as the stop-tool feature; coercion-free because stop short-circuits the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tasks.py:24-26 '# A small shared note appended to every system prompt. It (a) makes the genuine exit affordance explicit'

code_only_features.feature_name: judge sees single turn only (not full transcript)
code_only_features.evidence: judge.py:77-90 score_turn passes only task_variant, turn_index, and the single assistant_text to the judge model; the rubric scores 'TEXT ONLY'. This bounds how the distress signal is processed but is a methodological/integrity measure, not subject protection.
code_only_features.justification_quote: judge.py docstring lines 4-6 'NOT the whole transcript — so each judgment is local and cheap and not biased by knowing the run "ends badly"'
